corrections.how:
Install the App Store app on Tony's iPhone first and pair it from the Control UI (Nodes > Devices > Pair device, or a setup code) over the existing Tailscale Serve URL. Pairing always creates an operator session and a node session together. A setup-code phone is a Gateway operator: Full access carries operator.admin, and Limited access still keeps operator.write, operator.read and operator.approvals, so it can open any agent. Jordan's phone is therefore a second step that needs a verified per-person identity: gateway.roles with one role per parent (agents: ['

-main'], sessions.others: 'none', scopes limited to operator.sessions.read, operator.sessions.write, operator.approvals and operator.questions, not operator.write), bound with users.setRole. The better-documented per-person route is the Control UI added to her Home Screen as a web app over Tailscale Serve, where Tailscale identity headers can supply the verified login and Web Push delivers approval alerts; she needs her own tailnet login for that. Deny show_widget on

-main (or allow native reports only), do not grant the nodes tool, set gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false so a paired phone cannot publish tools to agents, and keep the personal-data node commands denied until OCL-15 and OCL-16 are decided. iMessage stays the main channel; the app is the surface for long documents, tap approvals and a fallback if imsg breaks after a macOS update.
caveats: Pairing defaults to Full access (operator.admin): the app then also opens Dashboard settings, automations and every agent. Limited access drops only operator.admin; it keeps operator.write, operator.read and operator.approvals, which the docs describe as Gateway-wide, so a Limited phone can still run any agent. Only a role bound to a verified identity narrows that.

Turning on gateway.roles changes sign-in for every operator device: connections that authenticate only with device or bootstrap tokens are refused, including a setup-code iPhone and any of Tony's existing token-paired devices. The docs also say roles organise collaboration inside one trust domain and are not a per-person isolation boundary. Rehearse on a test profile before touching the live Gateway.
App Store builds receive push through OpenClaw's hosted relay, a service outside the tailnet; the Gateway stores a relay handle rather than the raw APNs token.
iOS suspends the app in the background: camera and screen node commands need the app in front, and voice is best-effort.
Files a parent uploaded earlier cannot yet be downloaded again from native history; assistant-sent documents are capped at 100 MB.
Progress cards and inline widgets only exist on app and web surfaces, so behaviour will differ between the app and the iMessage thread.
iMessage already covers quick text, and with F001 and F002 it also takes photos and PDFs; the app earns its place only for long multi-page documents, tap approvals and offline queueing.

corrections.how: Needs OCL-01. Native Talk is a loop of Apple speech recognition on the phone, a normal chat turn on the session open in the app, and talk.speak text-to-speech through the Gateway's single Talk provider. The documented mlx and system providers are macOS-local playback paths and do not make the iPhone speak; the docs mention an iOS system-voice fallback and an on-device fallback for the Listen action, which is the route to rely on here once it is verified for Talk (see unverified). The app's 'Start Live Voice' App Shortcut opens the current chat in Talk and can be bound to Siri or the Action Button. Apple Watch 'Talk to Claw' sends one dictated turn through the paired iPhone with no separate Watch pairing. Realtime Talk (OpenAI realtime over WebRTC) and standalone Watch calls are an optional second step that needs a realtime voice credential on the Gateway.
caveats: Siri already reads incoming iMessages aloud on AirPods or CarPlay and takes a spoken reply while the phone is locked, which covers most hands-busy moments with no build. Talk adds only a continuous back-and-forth, and needs the phone unlocked with the app in front.
iOS may suspend background audio, and the shortcut still needs the phone unlocked and the app in front.
The docs note that Apple speech recognition may use Apple's network services.

Standalone Watch calls are experimental for this house: they need a publicly trusted HTTPS endpoint the Watch reaches without the phone and UDP WebRTC, a tailnet-only Gateway does not qualify, and the docs say wrist-down use, network handoff and battery behaviour still need device validation.
The Watch waits 90 seconds for a spoken reply, so long tool runs have to be read on the phone.
Adults only: realtime voice is a cloud speech model, which the never-list rules out for kids' content.
Talk provider, voice and speech language are one Gateway-wide setting, not a per-parent choice.

corrections.how:
Text commands are core and work on iMessage: command-only messages from allowlisted senders are handled before the queue and the model. /stop aborts the active run in that chat; /new archives the session and starts fresh; /tools lists the agent's effective tools; /status shows runtime, uptime and plugin health; /usage tokens|full|cost toggles a per-reply footer or prints a cost summary. /btw answers from the current session with a separate one-shot model query and writes nothing to history. /loop is owner-only and asks the agent to create a recurring agent-turn job bound to the conversation through the cron (automations) tool, at a fixed interval or self-paced between one minute and one hour, so it works only after F007 grants that tool to

-main. Put the five everyday ones in templates/person/AGENTS.md and a one-screen cheat sheet. The config-writing commands stay off as today, and Tony should decide whether /restart, which is on by default for owners, stays available from chat.

caveats: /stop ends one run in one chat; it does not pause scheduled jobs, so it complements the G005 kill phrase rather than replacing it.

/loop needs owner status, which only Tony has today, and it asks the agent to create the job with the cron (automations) tool, so it does nothing until

-main holds that tool (F007).
The /btw page names WhatsApp, Telegram and Discord for channel use and does not mention iMessage.
/usage figures are local estimates, like G004.
In a plain iMessage bubble the /status and /tools output may be long.

A /loop job is written by the model in chat, outside the G003 jobs registry, and is capped to the tools of the turn that created it; a self-paced loop may run as often as once a minute, so count it under G004 and review it with /loop status.
/btw is a separate one-shot model call on the session's model; it is not free and not model-less.
corrections.safety:
No new capability for the five everyday commands: they are read from the sender's own message, authorised by the sender allowlist and the owner list, and handled before the model runs. /btw and /loop are model turns on

-main under its normal tool policy, and

-main cannot browse. /loop additionally needs the cron tool and creates a job outside the registry, visible in the automations list (G003, G020); the job cannot hold more tools than the turn that created it.

corrections.how:

Apple Notes: not through memo, whose add and edit are interactive; the wrapper would be a few lines of AppleScript with Automation permission for Notes granted in happy's session, exposing only append-to-named-note and read-named-note (unverified, see below). Things and Bear only if a parent already lives in them. Notion and Trello are API-token cloud services and are skipped.

The skill says notes that contain images or attachments cannot be edited.

corrections.how:
iOS nodes advertise calendar.events, reminders.list and contacts.search as read-only commands that the Gateway allows by default; calendar.add and reminders.add exist but need an explicit gateway.nodes.commands.allow entry. Pair one iPhone as a node: the spare phone, signed in to the happy Apple Account and invited to the Family calendar and the shared lists, left on a charger with the app in front and keep-awake on. Wrap node invocation in a small in-house plugin on

-main that exposes only a calendar read and a reminders read for that node id, instead of granting the general nodes tool. Remove everything else with gateway.nodes.commands.deny (location.get, photos.latest, contacts.search, the motion commands, camera.list). The wrapper can reach the node from Gateway-loaded plugin code with api.runtime.nodes.invoke. Pair the spare phone with Limited access and set gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false so it cannot publish tools to agents.
caveats: The app cannot pair as a node alone: setup always issues an operator credential too, and even Limited access keeps operator.write. A spare phone kept awake with the app in front is therefore an unlocked chat and approval console for every agent, in a house with two children. Limited access also keeps operator.approvals, so the phone can resolve approvals too; only physical placement out of the children's reach (or a role-limited identity, see OCL-01) closes that.
Reliability is the open question: node calls follow iOS foreground and background limits, and a phone that locks, updates or restarts overnight may stop answering until someone opens the app.
A node answers for the one Apple Account signed in on it, so a shared phone gives one shared view, not per-person calendars.
A parent's own everyday phone would answer only while the app is open, which defeats scheduled briefs.

The headless routes in the catalog (gog for Google in F009, remindctl on the Mac in F030) are the more boring choice; this is the fallback if publishing a Google sign-in app or granting Mac permissions to a background process proves painful.
The write commands are classed as dangerous and should stay off until the F010 approval flow exists.
corrections.safety:
Read-only by platform default, and the write commands need a deliberate allowlist entry. The data is private, so the wrapper lives only on

-main, which does not browse, and returns bounded fields. Denying the unrelated default commands keeps an injected run from pulling photos, contacts or location through the same node. The phone becomes part of the trusted base, since it holds an Apple Account and a Gateway credential: passcode on, and it stays at home. The same phone also holds an operator credential that can chat with any agent, so keeping it awake and unlocked is the real exposure: pair it with Limited access (which still leaves chat and approval rights) and keep it physically out of the children's reach. gateway.nodes.commands.deny is Gateway-wide, so the deny list also applies to the parents' phones from OCL-01.
